title: Heating equal masses of materials
bodyMd:
Investigators heated three100g solid samples, designated P,Q and R, with identical constant-power electric heaters. Each sample began at20degrees C. The apparatus was insulated and heat losses were negligible over the interval shown. No sample changed phase. A sample's temperature rise for a given absorbed energy is inversely related to its specific heat capacity. The measurements are shown below.

| Heating time (s) | P temperature (degrees C) | Q temperature (degrees C) | R temperature (degrees C) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0|20|20|20|
|30|26|23|24|
|60|32|26|28|
|90|38|29|32|
|120|44|32|36|

Treat each trend as linear only for estimating temperatures or times within the observed interval. For a constant-power heater, equal heating times transfer equal amounts of energy to the samples.
